NGTeco Baby Monitor, Indoor Camera for Home Security, 1080P WiFi Monitor with Camera and Audio Dome Surveillance IP Camera for Dog/Pet/Nanny with PTZ Night Vision/Phone App/Cloud/SD Card Memory Set this camera up last night. The instructions are minimal but, enough to get it up and running.
Just had to download the app and register. Then plug the camera into an outlet. This is where it gets a little sketchy with the instructions. Have to play around with the app to figure out what you want on and what you want off.
The picture quality is fantastic. With the zoom part. I go to zoom and it's very sensitive. I went to enlarge the screen and I was immediately zoomed all the way in. Have to play around with it to get it just right.
The other thing I noticed, when playing around with the panning, is that it will rotate and I can see the ceiling but, I can't rotate it enough to where I can see the floor when it's on my fireplace mantle. So, I can't see where my dogs are when we're gone.
It does come with 2 screws, 2 mollies, and a small piece that you can put it up on the wall and then snap the main camera into the small piece that fits on the bottom part. I'll have to play around to see where the best place, for this camera, to sit so I can see more.
It's hard to judge night vision because we always leave a light on in our living room. So, it's not ever completely dark. But, with the one little light on, the picture is great and can see everything. And you can manually set it up for night vision or have it automatically switch to night vision. Great feature. You can also set up face recognition so it will know not to alert with the homeowners who are there all the time. Wow! Bad thing is, you have to pay for that part.
On the app, you'll see like a small pencil type thing in upper right corner. Tap on that to set up the basic settings. There is where you set settings like night vision, motion detection...etc.
The motion detection works great! But, tired of the alarms coming through my phone so I'm shutting it off until we leave the house.
This doesn't come with a micro SD card. I ordered one and waiting for it to come to put into this camera so I can store video for playback.
Really nice camera for babys room or like me, a home security camera.
text_fidelity_b: NGTeco Baby Monitor, Indoor Camera for Home Security, 1080P WiFi Monitor with Camera and Audio Dome Surveillance IP Camera for Dog/Pet/Nanny with PTZ Night Vision/Phone App/Cloud/SD Card Memory

While this isn't meant to be babyproof, I've found that the cage-like design and locking mechanism not only keep my cords tidier, but also makes them a lot less obvious and exciting to baby so that when it is placed out of reach, he isn't always clamoring to be lifted up to it, as he does with high-up cords that are not as hidden.

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. I also found the locking/ opening/ closing mechanism too stiff - in fact, I gashed my finger when it opened unexpectedly after having to push it harder than I should have to open it.

The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

Hour 15:
I am baffled by the positive reviews of this product. Yes, headphones and their sound signatures are very much a personal preference, but these are so grossly bad that I can only assume my ears are damaged or the headphones are defective. Returning them to Amazon.

SanDisk Ultra Fit 16GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive SDCZ43-016G-G46 I have a macbook pro with only 126gb of capacity in the SSD. This is not enough for someone who does photography and graphics design.
Unfortunately, with the new MBPs, apple decided that the user should not be allowed to change out their SSD for a larger capacity after purchase.
This caused a lot of problems and I was constantly transferring my images to an external HDD and it was extremely inconvenient.

I decided to purchase this USB flash drive. It was low cost for such a large amount of space. Best decision I ever made!
I have had this in my laptop for the last 2 months and it has not fallen out or gotten damaged. I carry my laptop everywhere with me.
Data transfers are very fast. With less than 50 picutures, it's basically instant and I often feel the need to check and make sure the files actually transferred because it happens so quickly, I don't even get a "Transferring files" window. I have never had a failed transfer.

If you are using it in a mac, you will need to reformat it to ExFAT. It will work out of the box, but will not accept large folders or files until it is reformatted.

The only issue I've ever had is if my computer falls asleep, the drive will sometimes disconnect, but that is due to the settings on my computer and not the drive. A simple unplug-replug reconnects it.

I bought this because the Mac Pro doesn't have an internal mic. Amazingly it also doesn't have a mic port. It has 3.5 mm headphones and speaker ports. I thought I could plug this into one of those ports. No luck.
The headset port apparently requires a 4 conductor 3.5 mm TRRS plug. Neither the computer maker nor the mic/headset maker ever give you this type of critical information. I probably should have purchased a USB mic instead. So now I either buy a USB mic or a USB adaptor.

My general comment about microphones and headsets is that the descriptions (both Amazons and the manufacturers) are almost always weak on connectors, adaptors and compatability (PC/MAC/etc). This is the most important feature and should be at the top of any description. After all if it doesn't fit or work what good is it.

The Wrap-It Storage Super-Stretch Silicone Bands caught my eye because of the bright colors and the ease of using them. It’s much easier to wrap a band around cords than to fumble with a cable tie.

The bands are about the same size as an average rubber band or ponytail, but they have less stretch. Which makes it hard to get the bands tight around a thicker cable, like an HDMI cable.

But otherwise, the Wrap-It bands are pretty good for organization. I like that I can organize cord type by color. In the 48 pack of bands, there are 6 of each color (red, salmon, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, and purple).

I wouldn’t recommend using these bands for ponytails unless you’re in a pinch, or have thin hair that needs the grip of silicone. My hair is thick, so these pull at my hair. The silicone also picks up loose hair and dust, so I’ll be sticking to using them for cables.

SAMSUNG 850 EVO 250GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-75E250B/AM) I have this in my gaming PC, though I didn't buy this on Amazon. I have several Samsung drives, they are the only brand of SSD's that I buy now for two reasons. Proven reliability, and Samsung Magician Software.

Speed wise any SSD is good. I also own a Crucial M500 that I installed in my Linux laptop with SATA I, which is reported to be much slower but in practice proved to be x10 faster than the original laptop hard drive. For all of my other computers what makes the Samsung nice is the software. With Samsung Magician Software I can adjust over provisioning and see if any updates are needed. It also gives you a lists (profiles) of some items that you might need to adjust in your OS to make the SSD run optimally. It will also show you the health status, how many writes have been made and it can do a speed benchmark (though this can be done by other free software too). Samsung also provides migration software, but I never used that since I prefer to install from scratch.

Of course the brand reliability is probably the most important. I wouldn't touch OCZ drives for example, even if they were free.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 850 EVO 250GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Internal SSD (MZ-75E250B/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
TiVo Roamio OTA 1 TB DVR - With No Monthly Service Fees - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player Overall it works well. And I love the no-monthly fee part of this unit. Though the unit runs slowly, as if it runs on a 1990-circa CPU.

The setup was super easy and straight forward. Picked up about 70 channels in the Denver market. (Didn't know there were that many.) Though half of them didn't actually broadcast anything. Then I had to narrow it down to about 10 channels that broadcast meaningful contents. It took a long time to download and apply updates during the initial setup. Took about 2 hours.

The menu navigates slowly. Each action took about 3-5 seconds for the unit to finish. The OnePass makes recording a series far more complicated than necessary. I have to jump through many hoops to make it happen. On my cable remote, I can simply press the record button twice to setup a series recording.

I really like how seamlessly TiVo integrates with my Netflix, Amazon Prime and Youtube accounts and leads me directly to the episodes. It is very convenient to use and it's quite a pleasant surprise.

My only gripe is when I view a recorded program and navigate the menu, I cannot exit the menu to go back to full screen viewing of my recorded program. The "back" button only backs out to the main menu. So I have to select the recorded program and resume viewing. For live TV, I can simply click on the "Live TV" button to go back to full screen viewing.

Despite its imperfection, the TiVo with no monthly fee is an outstanding value. For those who are looking to cut the cable or ditch the dish, this is the way to go.

[Update 2017.01.24] Downgrading from 5 to 3 stars. TiVo is supposed to do periodic updates only overnight, but two Sundays in a row, the unit attempted to perform updates during the day. The first update froze the unit so we missed 3 quarters of a NFL playoff game. The second time we caught it in time, so only missed a few minutes of another playoff game.
text_fidelity_b: TiVo Roamio OTA 1 TB DVR - With No Monthly Service Fees - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a:
Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black Some appear to have had some difficulty or confusion with assembly, but I did it solo fairly quickly with no issues and found the instructions very clear. No tools were needed and all of the pieces went on smoothly. The direction sheet clearly shows and lists what pieces to use. I guess some didn’t see that one of the shelf sections is thicker. The stand appears quite sturdy and stable. Yes, the only real issue is if you’re using the discs at the feet. I guess the bare, spike type feet ends are supposed to be for thick carpet. Like many I had mine on wood/laminate flooring and so need the small discs as the spike tips will surely scratch it up. This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. It definitely would’ve been nice if they’d just included both a spike and attached foot type tips with the stand especially at this price. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. It’s a shame they didn’t include a normal leg along with the pins. I still like the stand quite a bit, but I’d warn people with mobility issues against this one even as nice as it is.

I don't think it's notably brighter, though it is a different color. It is, however, way thinner, and has a smaller bezel. The magnets on the back are awesome for sticking it to something like a refrigerator. The stylus holder is a bit clunky, though a nice thing to have. Using the stylus as a kickstand is really weakly integrated.

If you just want to scribble some notes, or make some impermanent doodles, this is an awesome product. However, the product notes on this sales page say the following: "A free mobile app makes it easy to capture digital copies of your notes for easy sharing, editing and organizing." Yet my instruction manual makes it clear that there is NO way to transfer notes from the boogie board to any app or computer, so this claim is misleading and incorrect. I'm disappointed, as this ability to save notes is the only thing that made this a worthwhile upgrade from my previous model.

It depends on which specification it implements (these are 1.4) and what part of the specs the cable implements.

I'm very pleased with this device.

APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) this has nothing within Amazon's control! I have used APC UPSs at work for years and found them dependable, reliable for my 350+ server environment. Maybe their quality control doesn't extend to their consumer product line. upon install and following all instructions the battery failed self test, really!?!? it was manufactured 9/2103 passes their internal QA per document included in package but fails 3 months later????

update: 1/27/2014
did chat with APC support. I was told I should have plugged in UPS and charged battery for 16 hours PRIOR to attempting to put a load on it. NOTHING I have read in the accompanying documents even hinted to that. I am skeptical, but will do as instructed for process of elimination in troubleshooting this problem. I told the support rep that this little bit of information should be passed on to the END USER SOME HOW!! I will update this review as I go through the resolution of this issue.

update 1/29/2014
So I did what APC said and took the load off and charged the UPS for 24 hrs (I figured a little extra wouldn't hurt). Installed the UPS and placed a load on it (~35%), performed the self-test and it passed. This KEY IMPORTANT fact should be SOMEWHERE in the included documentation, it would help everyone! I did increase my rating since the product now works as described, not happy about the lack of documentation and extra hassle required kept my ratings from being higher.
text_fidelity_b: APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately)

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130) Arlo is not perfect, but it is wicked close.

What's Great: You can put it anywhere within range of the link/router. The alerts are reliable, if a little slow on the uptake. The picture is good. Set up was simple and worked the first time. A reasonable amount of cloud storage is free, and it's easy to download whatever you want to save. The cameras are easy to move around to wherever you need them, and you don't have to set them up again.

What's Okay: A person who walks fast can get through a room almost faster than Arlo can start recording. Now, it's still much faster than an old Belkin Netcam HD, which sends pictures of where the motion WAS. Before the picture. And the D-Link 930L, which is a fine monitor cam, but has never been able to send a snap or a clip, no matter how many times it has been set up to do that. However, both of those cameras have audio and stream reasonably good images via their apps (the Belkin video resolution is way better than the Dlink). That makes them okay monitors next to smart security sensors - if the sensor alerts, you can look to see what tripped it and listen to see what's going on. Arlo will - most of the time - catch whatever set it off and let you know within seconds. And it's free, not an extra $$$ feature.

What Could Be Better: The link thing is enormous. It could be a little less expensive. And it would be WONDERFUL if it integrated with Z-Wave or Smart Things. The plan here is to station the Arlo cams near other devices that send push notifications - Nest Alarms, Smanos smart sensors, etc.

How It Compares: Beats the Canary I couldn't get to activate. Way better than the other netcams in the house. Love it. Just added another camera.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130)

1080P HD Projector, 5G WiFi Movie Projector, UUO Home Theater Support 4K Video Projector, Synchronize Smartphone Screen, Dolby Audio Support-Compatible with TV Stick/iOS/Android/Smartphone/PS5 This is a decent entry level projector for every day use and a very good unit for specialized purposes like outdoor viewing on a large screen.

Its picture quality is better than most I have seen in this range and is brighter as well. The native 1080p image is sufficient for what you are buying, but one would never compare it to a higher end model. Of course, most of those start by adding another zero to the price, just for starters. I have had a couple of projectors in this price range and none of them really have a "great" picture, and that's honestly to be expected.

With this projector, you get a watchable image in daylight hours, but really improves if you black-out the room with darkening curtains or are watching after dark. The image will clearly show on a light color wall, but will improve drastically if you use an actual screen.

The fan noise is a little more intrusive than I would like, so it does interfere a bit if you are just using the included speakers. My suggestion is to connect it to a stand-alone external speaker setup. This is especially recommended if you are setting up an outdoor viewing screen.

It does tout 4D±50° Keystone correction, but it's not really as good as all that, in my opinion. I could never get the picture shape quite right at these angles. Connectivity is adequate, with several input options, so that's really a plus. I had it hooked up to an external hard drive as well as my Amazon Fire Stick and it handled each of them nicely. The WiFi connection is adequate and I had no issues connecting to my network. 5G connection is definitely a plus here as long as you are relatively close to your router.

Overall, I would say that this projector is a good value for the money spent. Try it out to see if Projection Television is for you. It's a whole new world, that's for sure. I don't miss going to the cinema as much anymore. Watching movies on the "Big Screen" at home is so convenient... and the popcorn is much cheaper.

text_fidelity_a:
GRADO SR80e Prestige Series Headphones The first thing I noted when I listened to these much-celebrated headphones (at least the Prestige line at any rate) is how incredibly exaggerated the low-end is. While getting that kind of bass response from a headphone driver is impressive, showing it off at the expense of fidelity is not something I particularly care for. When using these on a device where a DAC is involved, such as an iPad, I have to use the 'bass reducer' EQ profile on the device or the sound will otherwise will be muddy with distortion. I am sure this has a lot to do with the dinky amplifier inside the iPad being unable to fully drive the the whopping 32 ohms of resistance the SR80e pushes back with. As a rule, underpowered amplifiers are what ruin the drivers inside speakers or headphones so when you hear distortion it means your amplifier is underpowered when matched with the driver and you need to change one of those two things. When you hear distortion from a crappy amplifier that's the sound of your speakers being slowly ruined so you really want to avoid this. (I always have a sad chuckle when some punk is walking the streets with ghetto blaster at maximum volume and the sound is atrocious- little does he know that what people are annoyed by is not the volume, but the distortion! Plus he's ruining his equipment.)

Using the SR80e with a mobile device is a case where an external headphone amplifier would be highly desirable, if not required, so this is a bit of an ask. I have not had a lot of success with the in-line amplifiers designed to run off of the device's power (specifically the Lightning-DAC-and-amplifier combos that you can buy to replace the dongle that Apple ships with their new iPhones) where I played recordings which have very high amplitude levels. For these recordings, the distortion is intolerable even though records at a nominal recording level sound great. The lack of gain control is a real problem with these gadgets- something that is de-facto on any headphone amp that you don't put in your pocket. Therefore, you'll be reduced to using headphones like these at home or work, which is where I use mine.

The fact that you have to significantly alter the EQ profile of your audio player to even have these cans reproduce a sound that is remotely like the original recording violates "high fidelity" by definition. Compare this to a sound engineer style headphone set like Sony MDR Pros which are designed to reproduce the source signal as accurately as possible. This is what "high fidelity" actually means. Some people may not like this and will end up using some artificial bass boost on their device to compensate, which the MDRs will gladly deliver. Most people who listen to popular music are generally accustomed to excessive bass. If that is the sort of listener that you are, then these headphones are for you because once you get the SR80s tuned properly, the sound these cans deliver is very impressive. Very. Impressive.

Unfortunately, when using an IOS device, playing this profile with even high end earbuds like the UE Triple Fis, the sound will be tinny, so toggling between the two modes by way of a shortcut would be a nice bonus, but as it stands I have to go deep into the preferences to change this setting. Therefore, I would only recommend these headphones if you intend to use them in a stationary location. Since these are very high resistance earphones (even higher than most loudspeakers for that matter) you really ought to get an headphone amplifier if you want these to shine.

One other issue is with the minimalist foam cup pads. While they are comfy, they do not block sound in or out whatsoever, so if you use them in a noisy office you will be annoyed at how loud you have to play these to drown out ambient noise. Also, your workmates will probably be annoyed by the bleed through. I ended up getting a different cup pad kit which is marginally better, but it changes the fit somewhat so it takes a little fiddling to get them to sit on your skull around your ears evenly. Otherwise, the headphones are incredibly comfortable as they are very lightweight, which is surprising considering the size of the driver. Grado has found the sweet spot between having a massive (and heavy) drive coil magnet and being featherweight, even if I might take issue with their choices about fidelity reproduction.

Tl;DR: If you really like your sound overcharged with bass, these are the headphones for you. Otherwise, if you are looking for a quality but moderately priced pair of headphones, you might be better off with a more reference-style set like the Sony MDRs.
text_fidelity_b: GRADO SR80e Prestige Series Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507) Overall, this is a decent full-size USB keyboard. The keys are nicely sized and have a medium length throw. There’s little tactile feedback, making the keys feel rather mushy. But, on the plus side, it’s 100% silent in use – no clicky sound of any type.

The layout is a standard QWERTY with a separate number key pad and F1 to F12 at the top. There’s also a separate pad for cursor up/down/right/left.

The back light is very nice and has the unique feature in that you can change the color. There are several to pick from including a “mixed” mode that has several colors making for a rainbow look. Color selection is easy via a dedicated key at the top of the keyboard. Just press it to cycle through the colors. The back light can also be set to off.

The build quality is decent. It’s all plastic and pretty lightweight, but durable enough for normal use. There’s a kick stand on the back that folds out to prop up the keyboard at a comfortable angle, and non-skid feet to hold it in place. I had no problems with this staying put even when banging away at full typing speed. There is some flex in the frame when typing with force, but nothing horrible.

There’s a small area for resting your palm, but it’s rather short to provide much (if any) ergonomic support.

It does not have any indicator lights such as for caps lock, num lock, etc.

Installation is simple on a Win machine -- just a plug-and-play with no drivers needed.

While the overall design is nice and I love the back light feature (plus the ability to change colors), the lack of tactile feel and the lack of status indicator lights drops my rating to 4 stars. Still well worth considering as a replacement full-size USB keyboard, especially if you’re looking for a 100% silent keyboard.

text_fidelity_b: Azio PRISM USB Wired Keyboard with 7 Colorful Backlights, Black (KB507)

text_fidelity_a: HPRT MT800 Wireless Bluetooth Monochrome Portable Printer, Case+Cartridge+Printer，Supports 8.5" X 11" US Letter,Compatible with Android and iOS Phone, No-Ink Technology.(MT800QC) I have always wanted a little printer like this when I was working many years ago but they were never this small.  Now that I go camping in my RV and work while I camp I may want to print something without having to drag a full size printer along for the ride.  The price of this is on the high side even higher than the average full size printer so you better have a need to make it worth it.  Don't do what I did which was to unwrap everything before I ready the manual.  I thought I would have to install the enclosed ribbon but it is already installed at the factory and the one you see is a spare.  I decided to set it up to print from my phone since I mainly use a phone or tablet when on the road.  I downloaded the suggested app and it was easy to get started and I didn't need to sign up or register to do so.  My Bluetooth found it right away.  I selected first to print a photo file and selected low quality as I didn't want to waste ink.  It came out OK.  I next selected a page in a PDF manual that had a [photo embedded in it and selected medium quality and that turned out great.  The only gripe was it only gave me the following places to look for a file to print:  iCloud, Photo, Web and my print history.  I only had a couple things in iCloud as I mainly use Google Drive so I would have to move the document to iCloud first in order to print it.  Photo didn't allow me to browse my photos so I wasn't dure where to go there.  Once I printed a photo inn iCloud then that photo showed up there to print in the future.  I thought that was what the print history was for.  So, the app could use some UI work but I can't complain as everything worked/connected so easily.  Now, the paper.  You have to use their HPRT Premium Multi-Purpose Copy Paper.  It is a bit shiny on one side and more expensive than typical print paper.  This brings me back to you have to really need a niche printer like this to make it worth it.  I cannot sweat these things because I got it to use sparingly while I travel when something just has to be in print form.  I don't even really print much anymore from my home printer so once could say I waste cartridges there.  In summary, if you need a portable printer, that costs more with proprietary paper, for those short run printing emergencies on the road then this is great.  It works great and is easy to setup.
text_fidelity_b: HPRT MT800 Wireless Bluetooth Monochrome Portable Printer, Case+Cartridge+Printer，Supports 8.5" X 11" US Letter,Compatible with Android and iOS Phone, No-Ink Technology.(MT800QC)

text_fidelity_a:
Nexus 7 from Google (7-Inch, 16 GB, Black) by ASUS (2013) Tablet I received the Nexus 7 as a gift this year for Christmas, and so far I am quite pleased with it. Having a Galaxy Nexus phone, I felt quite comfortable with navigating and configuring the Nexus 7. It's very convenient to be able to share so many apps between my phone and this tablet. The Nexus 7 seems like it's very well built. It has just enough heft to not feel cheap, and the rubberized backing has a nice grip (though this won't matter to most, since a case will likely be the first accessory anyone buys.) The display is wonderful, and has quite a large viewing angle. For such small speakers, I'd say that the Nexus 7 sounds pretty good. I've only charged the device twice, since 12/24, and it gets used quite a bit.

So far, I've used the Nexus 7 for watching videos online (YouTube, Netflix, HBO Go,) streaming music from Amazon Prime, browsing the web, some light gaming with Final Fantasy Dimensions, chatting and computing (Maxima for Android and Wolfram Alpha) and I would say that it's handled everything I've thrown at it like a champ.

The only other tablet I own is a Kindle Fire HD 8.9", which works quite well for reading my technical PDFs, but seems to lack in the other "tablet" departments. I have used an iPad or two in the past. I would have to say that the Nexus 7 is by far my favorite tablet so far.

I'm currently using an Armorsuit screen protector and a Moko slim case that folds into a stand, and would recommend both accessories. I ordered a blue tooth keyboard. I'm hoping that the Nexus 7 with a keyboard might replace my aging netbook.
text_fidelity_b: Nexus 7 from Google (7-Inch, 16 GB, Black) by ASUS (2013) Tablet

THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology I've tried some low-cost in-car cams and have been unimpressed with the build quality or video quality of the devices. The Thinkware 550 was a marked departure - it feels very well-built and solid. I'd rate the build quality up there with a decent conventional camcorder, such as a Sony. It also looks very attractive - they did a great job with the design.

This is not an "action cam" type of device for uploading videos of during stupid stuff onto Youtube (sorry, showing my age here - I probably would have done the same had cams been around in my youth). Rather, it's a cam for automatically documenting events that occur while driving (such as a crash or other incident) without any need for user action. Video files are time and date stamped, and assigned a location using GPS. It's more of a "black box" type recording device for a car rather than a "fun time" action cam with a car mount.

You can also use this while parked and with a rear camera, but both of those require additional items not included with this package (hard wire install for parking use; a separate camera for rear view use).

Installation is easy but also a little bit tricky. The mount is a plastic cradle with an adhesive backing. Once you determine where you want the cam mounted (up on the windshield is the recommended position) you peel off the backing on the adhesive pad and stick it to the windshield. It's a permanent mount (well, you can remove it from the glass, but it can't be reused). Easy to do, but tricky in that you really need to take some time before committing to a location and think through where the power cord needs to be routed.

The unit is lightweight (5.1 ounces without the cradle) and seems to be holding well to the windshield even over very bumpy terrain.. The manual suggests leaving the cam off the cradle until the adhesive has cured for 24 hours. I didn't see that tip until after I tested its holding ability over broken road. So if you miss that tip as well, it doesn't seem to be a problem.

The cam does not have a built-in battery. It must be powered by an included cigarette lighter adapter (known by "power ports" these days, but I still call them cigarette lighters). The adapter is very nicely made with a stout cord. That's good for longevity; not so good for routing it so the cord is not visible or in the way. There are some adhesive tabs included to lasso down the cable to help make for a neat (or semi-neat) install. I'll probably add some electrical tape to neaten up the install a bit more.

The manufacturer also cautions to make sure the power port you use gets shut off when you turn off the engine. The cam can continue to pull power if the power port is live, potentially draining your car's battery.

It automatically powers up when you start the car. It can be manually turned off (or back on) as well. It offers two recording modes: continuous (which is in one minute segments) or on-demand (you can manually start and stop). It also states that when there is an impact, the cam will store the 10 seconds before and the 10 seconds after in a secure memory folder. I'll have to take their word for that - can't really test that out! Under normal circumstances, when the micro SD card fills up it starts overwriting old files.

A micro SD card is included along with a reader. The card holds the user manual and the software, so it can't really be used to store video files. I used my own card reader rather than the one included since the included one was too tiny for my clumsy fingers to deal with.

There is no viewer on the cam - you have to take out the SD card and pull up the files using the included software. That for me is the biggest problem and limitation of this device. You have to trust that it's working since there's no confirmation other than the indicator lights and prompts. Nor can you set the camera specs unless you have access to a PC.

On the plus side, the lack of a screen means there's no risk of driver distraction while the cam is operating. I can't fault that. Still, I would have liked to see a design that has a screen that remains off until the camera is out of the mount so it can be used in-car to change settings or review stored video. That maintains the lack of driver distraction but still allows for better use of the cam while parked.

What makes up for a lot of these shortfalls is the video quality. Great - really great. Crisp, clear and sharp. It provides a panoramic view (the specs say 140 degrees) that easily covers the full view from the windshield. You really won't believe this is from a car cam. It dealt with head-on full sunlight pretty well, and did a decent job at night. I did get a fair amount of reflection off the windshield at night, but the video was very workable.

The included software installed fine on a Win 7 machine after I suspended Avast from running - this software does not want to work and play well with Avast. I even had to keep Avast suspended while running the software. Not tough to use - got the hang of it from just trying out menu options and playing around. It will ask to install an update right off the bat.

The video quality and overall "forget about it and it just records" type of operation are strong pluses. The power cord, mounting system, and lack of a view screen are problems. Weighing everything together gets me to a 3.5 star rating which I'll round up to 4 stars since the video quality is so nice. If you can live with the limitations, this is well worth considering.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE F550 Full HD Dash Cam with high-speed Cortex A8 Processor, GPS Tracker & Dual Save Technology

I really wanted just a plain old back up, but having an Electronics Engineering degree, I had to stay current. I had my Kindle HD out in the yard, playing music right off of MBL, while I do my gardening (downloaded the free app for Kindle). It was cool. I feel it will probably be short lived. Last year I bought a cheap WiFi receiver and it was so fast, this year it is so slow. I don't have high expectations from WiFi, and this drive only has the capability to plug into the network. It does not have USB connectivity at all. I do often times want a quick and easy way to transfer files to my new computer, while I do other things. The price was not too bad, but for that money I hope to be able to recover my data even after the WiFi dies. A good back up drive from WD usually last for years. That is what customers are accustomed to anyhow. I will probably update this review in one year. I did password protect my drive before the first file ever got added. I did update the firmware also. So far it is a nice thing to have.
My update on this drive is that it gets better as I use it. I don't know why that new things on my network start out slow and speed up as they are used, but it is working well.

text_fidelity_a: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) This unit does work, but it is too slow for me to recommend it to others. When writing music onto it from my Windows computer, the write speed was slow enough to repeatedly drop the data transfer rate all the way to zero. Other manufacturers' flash drives do not do that; they keep on going. The read speed is slow enough that it causes my car's infotainment system (2019 model year) to sometimes hang up. Indeed, at one point, it caused my backup camera to go to all black for a minute or two. Note that some other reviewers are apparently unware of what flash memory is like. It has a limited number of times that it can be written (rewritten), and it will wear out if you try to use it as a substitute for a SSD. It also isn't going to be nearly as fast as a SSD. Flash memory is most appropriate for putting mp3 files into your car's infotainment system and other applications that are write only a few times but read many times.
text_fidelity_b: SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker Overall, I'm pleased with this speaker. It hits the mark where it counts the most -- great sound. It makes the audio output of the Kindle Fire sound SO much better!

I also like that it runs on removable batteries. Many of the other small speakers I looked at had an internal rechargeable battery. While that has some advantages, the fact that the Fire does not have a USB port means I'd have to charge them from an outlet (with an adapter) or on my PC. Plus, non-removable batteries can present a problem when they fail. The Altec Lansing uses 3 AAA batteries which are far easier to deal with. I still use rechargeables (either Eneloops or the Amazon Basic rechargeable) and get several hours of play time per charge.

The shortcomings relate to the cord. It's short (about 8 inches) and is very thin. It would be a much better product with a longer cord (about 12 inches) and a cord that's made of more substantial material. I can see the cord being a potential point of failure down the road due to its lightweight construction.

But overall, it's a good device and a great value (if you catch it on a price dip). Highly recommend as an add-on to the Fire.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic VIERA TC-P50GT30 50-Inch 1080p 3D Plasma HDTV For the price, this is the 3D plasma to own. Panasonic makes the highest rated, best plasma displays on the market for the middle-end consumer and even higher-end sets. The GT30 has taken some hits due to its black-leveling during scene transitions. This seems most notable to those who may not understand or have the know how to alter the video settings properly; I DID notice this occurring when video output is set to "standard", once you tune the display properly, there should be no noticeable or any flickering between darker scenes to brighter transitions. To go into great detail on how to properly set your TV would be worthless, a "good" picture varies person by person but this preliminary issue should not deter one from purchasing this set.

With that out of the way, consider this: you will not see a better high definition plasma display on the market. At the GT30 price, you are not going to get 3D quality, HD quality, feature set and value any where else. If you have not been to any store to view other brands competing with this set/price, do so and do yourself a favor. Once you see a GT30 set up properly, showing the same content as other brands, there should be no questions left to answer. The display owns. From blu rays to PS3 to Wii to regular DVDs, I have not scene until this plasma a more OUTSTANDING visual display. Blu Rays appear as though people are standing in your living room.

the most noticeable attribute of this plasma, at least to me, is the quality and richness of the depth in the display. Its simply amazing. Looks like you can reach your hand into the background and touch things. And no, I am not talking about when 3D is on, that is another story. In pure HD form without 3D, the depth, black, and richness of this display is simply jaw dropping. Your friends will not understand what they are looking at. To note, a HD gaming system looks simply unbelievable. You will be playing your games for the "first time" all over again.

The bad: THE SPEAKERS ARE DOWN RIGHT AWFUL. if you do not have some sort of surround sound system, or at the very least two channels (front left/right) the speakers sound terrible, they may as well sold it without them and saved a few bucks. You will need some sort of sound bar or extra components to get anything other than dialog. And the dialog is barely satisfactory; no bass, tiny highs, bad spacing and underpowered.

3D: Panasonic has the best 3D on the market. Compare it with Samsung or Sony. There is no comparison. View them back to back and you will find that Panasonics 3D technology, although requiring ACTIVE shutter glasses, reproduced 3D images in HD form where as others may not. Samsung for example, 3D reproduction looks like cardboard paper cutouts with no depth and lacking resolution. Not in the GT30 however. The 3D is amazing and even the 2D->3D reproduction (taking standard 2D video and artificially creating 3D images) adds incredible depth to your viewing experience, albeit not so much "pop" off the screen. Worthy to note is that 3D viewing does produce a somewhat dimmer display, not sure if this is due to the glasses tint or how their system works, but overall when 3D is on, expect a less vibrant picture from non-glasses viewing.

Overall, theres not much out there for the GT30 price that offers screen size, content and value. Above all else, picture quality should take the cake here. Please check it out in a store and make your decision. Cant beat this set. On a side note, internet connectivity works flawlessly, I wired the TV with a ethernet cable, which, you should do if you expect the highest speeds and purest connection. The TV synced up with zero glitches and loaded youtube, pandora and amazon with the ease of touching 1 button.

Excellent buy, sound is its largest demerit but can be remedied for a couple of bucks. Good luck!!
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic VIERA TC-P50GT30 50-Inch 1080p 3D Plasma HDTV

House of Marley Uprise: Wireless Earphones with Microphone, Bluetooth Connectivity, 8 Hours of Playtime, and Sustainable Materials (Teal) I have a lot of styles of headphones, and I now know what this type is perfect for: exercising. Maybe you and everyone else already knew this. But if I'm running (or elliptical-ing), regular ear buds may fall out, and bigger headphones can fall off or at least get uncomfortable sweaty. Obviously, you don't want a cord connected to your phone for exercising, so these hit the sweet spot in all those ways.

They are very comfortable as well. The ear pieces that come connected are a perfect fit for my ears, and already offer real sound-proofing from the outside world (warning: you may appear to be an annoying millennial if you walk around isolated from the world with these all the time). They are comfortable, and I love the easy way that the ear-hanger pieces are removable. I also like that you can tighten up the connecting strap. There must be a cable in there, so I hope it doesn't wear out this way, but it seems to be pretty durable, so I guess it will be okay.

Actually, these are great. The charging area is barely large enough for the micro-USB port, but the battery lasts for quite a few hours. Not as long as some headphones, but the low weight is key here.

Also good for: watching movies or listening to music on planes if you have your own device. No cord to slow you down when a seat-mate wants to get past you, and they're comfortable enough to fall asleep in, unlike over-the-head headphones.

Oh, I saw a review that said the bass was poor. I do not agree. Music sounds great in these. They can operate on low power because they are so far up in your ear. Be careful to keep them at a reasonable level.

I would recommend these to friends.
text_fidelity_b: House of Marley Uprise: Wireless Earphones with Microphone, Bluetooth Connectivity, 8 Hours of Playtime, and Sustainable Materials (Teal)

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird Freedom Sprint Bluetooth Headphones - Retail Packaging - Midnight Black Overall I'm very pleased with these ear buds. They are my first pair of bluetooth buds and it has been wonderful to not have to deal with cords, especially when working out. I can't tell you how many times I've hit an earbud cord while exercising and ripped the ear bud from my ear. A real pain in the neck (and ear!).

>>>Pros:

Comfort - These fit very well in my ear. There are different tip sizes to create a good fit and, after trying them all out, I went with the medium size. Very comfortable to wear even for long periods of time.

Stay put - I've yet to have them fall out even when doing aerobic exercises or while on the treadmill.

Sound - they sound pretty good. The sound is not as good as my favorite (and inexpensive) corded buds ([[ASIN:B0053R0WWG RHA MA-350 Aluminium Noise Isolating In-Ear Earphones]]) but they are a solid B+ performer with regard to bass response and overall clarity. Keep in mind that good bass response is affected by how the buds fit in your ear, so it's important to try out different tip sizes to see how they affect sound quality. They do get harsh at loud volumes, but for normal listening they are more than fine for my non-audiophile ears. They do reasonably well at blocking out ambient noise.

Setup - I found it straightforward even though I've never had any experience with setting up bluetooth earbuds.

Size - nice and compact so you don't get the "radar dish" look that larger units can have.

Durability - they have a "sweat proof" guarantee which is nice (although I imagine, like most guarantees, there are some loopholes). Overall build quality is good, with a very solid feel to all components.

>>>Cons:

Battery life - The manufacturer claims a battery life of 4.5 hours but I've yet to get more than 3 hours off a single charge. Plus there's no warning about battery life (until you're almost fully discharged) or a visual indicator of how much charge there is left.

Usability - the buttons on the buds are too small, making it difficult for me to push the right one. A lot of fumbling and mis-presses, making it often easier to deal with volume changes on the device, which kills some of the value of having wireless buds. I guess I lack the nimble fingers of the primary target market.

But overall, I'm pleased. The pros outweigh the cons, and I think this is a solid 4-star device.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird Freedom Sprint Bluetooth Headphones - Retail Packaging - Midnight Black

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic LUMIX DC-ZS70S, 20.3 Megapixel, 4K Digital Camera, Touch Enabled 3-inch 180 Degree Flip-front Display, 30X LEICA DC VARIO-ELMAR Lens, WiFi (Silver) Oct. 2020: If you're photographing foliage with a lot of stems & leaf edges, turn off/down i.Resolution. The "i" isn't that intelligent & makes some nasty over-sharpened halos in some spots. My advice, if you like the overall look of the jpeg, shoot raw+jpeg & process the raw using the jpeg as a guide. This isn't needed all the time. Only some scenes have this problem.
8/14/2020 I never played with the weird 4K burst modes. I just mucked with them today. They tend to hang up the camera. They don't seem to offer much over the regular drive modes. They take up two programmable buttons I can put to better use.
7/18/2019 Low light. No camera of this type is going to do well in natural light at last light (9 PM here.) This one is noticeably worse than my SX720HS. And that's bad.
6/29/2019 With an upgraded SD card, I tried the high speed video. The 240 fps VGA mode worked like a dream. To access it, you have to have the camera on [Cinema Camera]M mode. WARNING: Objects in camera fall 1/8th as fast as real life. :)
6/24/2019. With hundreds of pictures down, I really like the flip screen. I also like the auto bracket. I tend to keep it on 1/3 stop; 2/3 seems to be a bit wide. I've turned off the touch screen. Moving the focus position with the tip of my nose whenever I use the EVF is right out.
6/21/2019. Video playback seems to be twitchy on this model. Apparently some cameras, some times have trouble playing back some videos. Check your memory card specs. Even with a high end card, playback is chancy. Recording is fine. Playback on a PC is fine.

6/17/2019. The only serious negative about this camera is the slight increase in size and weight over my old SX720HS. It's about twice the volume. It has reasons for that, with the added features, particularly the tilt-screen and the EVF.

I really like high-end, 1/2.3"-sensor, long-zoom, point & shoot cameras. This one is pretty close to the limit. Much more and you have to go to 1" sensor designs, which hurts your zoom range. I currently have:
-Canon SX280HS--great camera, still has features no one else has, terrible for videos (I don't care), battery hog (I do care)
-Canon SX720HS--basically the SX280HS perfected. I wouldn't normally upgrade this soon, but for,
-Panasonic ZS70--this camera, which I got for very short money (thanks Amazon warehouse)

* I wasn't that interested in the flip-up screen, I don't do selfies or vlogs. Boy was I wrong. It allows you to snake the camera into positions that would otherwise require a contortionist.
* I was interested in the EVF. It's good in dim light, but I'm used to eyeballing pictures from an external screen. Still a plus, but less of one than I thought.
* I was interested in the powerful bracketing functions. Still interested, but I'll need a bit more study to make it work.

Generally, I shoot in P mode or M mode. Both modes work fine on this camera. The autofocus is better than on the two Canons. The focus modes take a little experimentation to find the one that works best for you, but they all seem to work. 'Standard' color balance is fine. I need to play with 'Natural' a bit to see which one I prefer. The attached photos were all taken on standard. All on a single sunny morning walk after a rainy night in Massachusetts.

First impression? This is a really good camera, even at the list price.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic LUMIX DC-ZS70S, 20.3 Megapixel, 4K Digital Camera, Touch Enabled 3-inch 180 Degree Flip-front Display, 30X LEICA DC VARIO-ELMAR Lens, WiFi (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

ZAGG Limitless, Full-Size Multi-Device Universal Bluetooth Backlit Keyboard - Black I've been getting to the point where I have multiple tablets and mobile devices around the house that occasionally benefit from having a physical keyboard. I like that this one lets me switch between three paired devices with the push of a button.

It feels sturdy and the keys have a pleasant texture. It's bigger than previous bluetooth keyboards I've tried, which I think is in keeping with it being designed to be used with multiple devices. It's also kind of heavy, so it seems more like an around the house keyboard than a portable.

I like it better as an occasional keyboard than one to use all the time. it's too flat to feel ergonomic. The alt and command keys on the bottom row are all double size, which feels like a designer wanted a big space bar but didn't want to leave any empty space anywhere. The result is that they are easy to bump, which can send you off into menus. The slot for standing up a device on the back of the keyboard feels a bit close, and not wide enough for my Surface tablet in landscape mode, and portrait mode makes it fall over, so the stand is likely only good for things up to small tablet size.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver I wanted a set of speakers to use mainly for my Kindle Fire and MP3 player, but also as my computer speakers. Due to space constraints, a 2.0 system was my only option, since a subwoofer (regardless of the size) would be problematic.

So the search began. There were several speakers that sounded great, including the Creative Gigaworks, M Audio and Audioengine. However, they lacked the convenience features I wanted such as ease of connecting/disconnecting a tablet and volume control without having to reach out and touch the speaker.

The Bose Companion 20 initially caught my eye because of the control pod. That was a great solution to my problems since I could control the volume right on my desk plus have the ability to plug in/unplug a tablet very easily. The sound quality sealed the deal - everyone who hears these speakers think they are a 2.1 set due to the ample bass. But, the bass is not at the expense of clear mid and upper ranges.

I use these 60% for music and 40% for video, and for both applications, the sound quality has been just wonderful. I'm also impressed that they sound just as good with the volume dialed way down as they do at moderate or blast-out-the-walls loud.

The control pod is very well made. It has a nice weight to it and a non-skid backing so it stays put. The volume control works very smoothly with a solid feel. I'm especially fond of being able to turn the speakers on and off by just touching the control pod.

You can connect it to the PC and to an aux device (such as a tablet) and use both at the same time. That's important since I want to listen to music or a video from my Fire, but still want to hear a chime when an email arrives.

My complaints are that the control pod cable is a bit too short for my needs. It's about 5 foot long, which is ample if you have the speakers next to your PC, but I have my speakers on a shelf above my desk. I was able to arrange things to make it work, but another foot or two of cable (or the ability to purchase an extension) would have been nice. It's a custom cable, so an off-the-shelf extension is not possible.

My other complaint is the price. I was able to get a used pair for half of the regular price. I think these are a bit overpriced at the regular price. But, Bose hit a really unique niche - the ability to have great sound without any compromise in convenience. If you want both, there's a high cost for admission.

If the price is not an issue, these very much deserve a hard look if you're in the market for a great sounding pair of 2.0 speakers. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)

ANTOP Omnidirectional HDTV Antenna Smartpass Amplified Outdoor 55/65 Miles Long Range AT-414B I've been collecting random TV antennas for review and from yard sales for years, and I think I've had about a dozen now. I generally only keep the two best ones. I tested this one out against my previous champion, which was just a single heavy duty rabbit ear on a magnetic base that somehow beat bigger, newer, and powered models.

The first thing I did with this when I got it was take it apart. I've gotten some in the past where the big plastic dish parts were just plastic for show and had nothing in them. Inside this one were multiple omnidirectional antennas and a circuit board. After attaching it to the coax, I checked through my channels and noticed I was missing some. I then added in the powered section, but didn't turn it on. This totally switched which channels I was missing. Then I turned it on and I got all my channels, plus another one I hadn't previously gotten, so it wins. The various parts do actually do something.

The pictures don't give much idea of scale. It's about the size of a steering wheel and comes with mounting plate. It's kind of huge and I wasn't pleased when I saw the size, but hey, I'll take the size if I get a brand new channel out of the deal.

I received a sample for review but the opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: ANTOP Omnidirectional HDTV Antenna Smartpass Amplified Outdoor 55/65 Miles Long Range AT-414B

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors) This jumpdrive is USB 3.0 (fast) but backward compatible with 2.0. It's a little cheesy looking because of its plastic "bubblegum" look, but the color-coding of the different size drives could be useful. I got the bright green 32 GB USB 3.0 stick for review, and when I put it into my USB port it showed installation files on the drive for both Windows and Mac. I double-clicked the Mac for my MacBook Pro, and it presented me with the installation screens. It was a little confusing how to get the software installed, and initially I had to install it on my computer to access the installation for just the flash drive; it's supposed to be optional to install it on your computer, but it wasn't apparent how to bypass computer installation. I had to delete my computer vault after it was created to get it off my computer.

Another confusion is that you are taken to a website with an offer for an Encryptstick software upgrade for a reduced cost or free for a 14-day trial. Apparently, all the best features of this device are not available if you just use the stick as a USB drive with the standard "Encryptstick Lite" app that comes with it. You will have AES encryption, but not the "military grade encryption," whatever that means. (The website lists the option to encrypt vaults with 128, 256, or 512-bit AES ciphers [1024-bit coming], registered and government approved, FIPS 140-2 compliant). Here are the other features listed on the website and, again, it's not clear which come with the standard installation and which with the upgraded one:

Runs on Multiple OS computers and all recently made USB flash drives
Encrypt & Decrypt Your Private Files
Easy to Use Encryption Interface [debatable!]
Speedy Auto-Updater
Lost Flash Drive Data Recovery Feature
Advanced Virtual Keyboard
Lock out Computer Installation is Optional - Not Essential
Lock out No Admin Rights Required
File Wipe Instant Lock
Quick Search, Live Search
Automatic Timeout
Limited Login Attempts
File Wipe File Shredder

I went on and purchased the upgrade (12.99 to Lexar users instead of the usual 39.99) because the advanced backup features are only available with the upgraded version and I did want them, but I thought it was a little sneaky how they presented all this. It's really not clear that you don't have to get the upgrade to make the stick itself work. Once you've purchased the upgrade, you are given links to download the upgrade for all versions (PC, Mac, and Linux) in an email.

Somehow I wound up with both the EncryptStick Lite and EncryptStick apps both running at the same time. I could not close out of either one of them, and attempting to eject the jumpdrive gave me an error saying I needed to close out of both apps. I had to force-quit the Lite app. That made me nervous about the whole thing.

I have to mention the following experience because, for me, it was an issue. The little lanyard (about the length of the drive when installed) is not attached when you take it out of the package, and I had a heck of a time getting it threaded through the end. The cord won't bend through the jumpdrive's hole, so it requires using an implement of some come to grasp the thread end and pull it through. My tweezers were too large, and so was the end of the large paperclip (all I had), so I wound up having to strip off the coating on an old bobby pin that I just happened to have lying in a drawer. Even then, I had to pop up part of the plastic cover on the front of the drive case a little to work the thread through, and I was worried about destroying the drive in the process. This whole process was very aggravating, so I think it would be better if they sold these with the lanyard already attached. Customers can then remove it if they don't want it, but I think the lanyard is quite useful. If you have more than one of these drives, you could hang them all up on a keyholder at your desk, then pull one off to take with you as needed.

Please note that I am downrating this product because of the initial confusion and hassles above, although in fairness this is not a good indication of the reliability and performance of the jumpdrive once the software and lanyard are installed. Consider this review to be of the initial experience with the jumpdrive and software. If I discover any more problems as I use this drive over time, I will come back and post them. For now, though, I'm tired of fooling with it!
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S35 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - LJDS35-64GABNL (Assorted colors)

HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A) This is a great improvement over an earlier-gen ZINK paper ("zero ink") portable printer we have, which requires a wired connection and a proprietary charger, and no longer holds a charge well.

The HP Sprocket connects and prints wirelessly, charges from a standard micro-USB cable, and has a lithium-ion battery which is sure to last a lot longer.

We had it unboxed and printing in less than 5 minutes. You run it from a free app available for Android or Apple iOS devices. We used the Android version and it works great.

It takes less than 30 seconds to wirelessly send and print a photo. The prints are 2 inches by 3 inches, smooth and glossy, good resolution, and have a peel-and-stick backing for quick and easy mounting. In the long run, the priciest thing about a ZINK printer is the paper, so shop around for deals.

The prints came out a little to the warm side in color when sent "as is," but the app allows a lot of enhancement and has lots of effects you can add.

The Sprocket printer itself measures only 3 inches by 5 inches and less than an inch thick, and weighs about 6-and-a-half ounces. It's very portable.

And it's loads of fun.
text_fidelity_b: HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A)

Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black) I've been using a Linksys router for years and it never missed a beat (their wireless G model with the two antennas). But, after upgrading my Internet from DSL to cable, I thought a new router would be in order.

Before buying one I searched for reviews from computer and tech magazines/sites. Talk about confusing! I'd read one review that gave a sterling endorsement for a particular router; then another review from another site that gave the same router a horrible review.

Since my router needs are pretty basic (just use it to share Internet access) I concentrated on ease of install issues. In that regard there was consensus about how easy Linksys is to install. So I went with them again, and selected the 1200 model since it gave me all that I wanted/needed at a good price (but, to hedge my bets, I got it at a warehouse club so I could return it easily).

So happy with this router! Installation was SO simple -- if you can plug in a cable you can install this router. But, should you want to tinker with settings, you can also access the full, detailed configuration menu and tweak settings to your heart's content. I think it took me longer to open up the box and unwrap the router and power cord than it took to actually get it to work.

Performance so far has been excellent. I put it on the ground level of my house and have no problems getting a strong signal in the basement and upper level. I did find that it helps to put the router in the middle of the house rather than against a wall for best signal strength throughout the house.

Considering that my Linksys G is still cranking along after several years, I'm reasonably confident (or at least hopeful) that this will last me an equal length of time.

If you're looking for a solid, easy to install single band router, this is it. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black)
